title: Perinatal Exposure to Traffic-Related Air Pollution and Atopy at 1 Year of Age in a Multi-Center Canadian Birth Cohort Study.
ehr_evidence: The CHILD study (http://www.canadianchildstudy.ca) is a prospective longitudinal national birth cohort that recruited over 3,600 families between 2008 and 2012 in four Canadian cities.
summary: Prospective multi-center birth cohort study examining the association between perinatal traffic-related air pollution (NO2) exposure and atopy at 1 year of age in Canadian children.
key_findings: TRAP exposure after birth increased risk for atopy to any allergens (aOR = 1.16 per 10 μg/m3 NO2; 95% CI: 1.00, 1.41).
No association was found during pregnancy (aOR = 1.02; 95% CI: 0.86, 1.22).
Association was stronger among non-daycare attendees (aOR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.28, 2.01) compared to daycare attendees (aOR = 1.05; 95% CI: 0.81, 1.28).
Positive but non-significant trends were found for food (aOR = 1.17; 95% CI: 0.95, 1.47) and inhalant allergens (aOR = 1.28; 95% CI: 0.93, 1.76).
captured_features: Maternal atopy, asthma, smoking, and SES
population: 2,477 children approximately 1 year of age from four Canadian cities
limitations: Exposure assessment derived from modeled estimates rather than direct measurements
Reliance on self-reported environmental and parental risk factors
Cohort bias toward higher socioeconomic status
Infiltration model developed for US cities applied to Canadian homes
Missing covariate data reduced sample sizes for some analyses
Lack of sufficient power for certain subgroup analyses
